payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth, the Name has the Mother of all things. The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits. These two are one in origin but different in name. They are both called the "Mysterious" (Xuan). The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: the Name has the Mother of all things
issues.advice: The source 有名萬物之母 means 'the Named is the mother of all things'; the translation reverses the relation and omits 'is'.

issues.span: The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 lacks an explicit subject; rendering it as 'The Way' adds a subject not in the text. Better to keep the subject implicit or use 'one'/'we'.

issues.span: the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 is a nominal phrase ('the Nameless: the beginning of Heaven and Earth'); adding 'is' is acceptable but should be consistent with the parallel clause.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Mysteries
issues.advice: This is a fragment without a verb; integrate into the previous sentence or supply a predicate to match the source's parallel structure.

issues.span: the "Mysterious" (Xuan)
issues.advice: Glossing 玄 as 'Mysterious' is acceptable, but the capitalized noun and parenthetical romanization are inconsistent with the rest of the rendering; consider a consistent term such as 'the Mystery'.

payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth, the Named is the mother of all things. The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits. These two are one in origin but different in name, both called the Mystery. The Mystery is the Mystery again and again; the Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits.
issues.advice: The source says '常無欲以觀其妙常有欲以觀其徼' — the subject is the observer (one who is constantly without desire / with desire), not 'the Way' itself. The translation wrongly makes the Way the subject of seeing. Render as 'One who is constantly without desire observes its wonder; one who is constantly with desire observes its limits.'

issues.span: The Mystery is the Mystery again and again
issues.advice: '玄之又玄' means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'more mysterious still', not a repeated assertion 'is the Mystery again and again'. Use 'mystery upon mystery' or 'ever deeper mystery'.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Mysteries
issues.advice: '衆妙之門' is conventionally 'the gate of all wonders' / 'the gateway to all marvels'. 'Many Mysteries' is nonstandard and shifts '妙' (wonder/marvel) to 'mystery', conflating it with '玄'.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: This is a sentence fragment with no main verb; integrate it as '...the gateway to all wonders.'

issues.span: The Way
issues.advice: '道' as 'The Way' is acceptable, but note the capitalized 'Name'/'Nameless'/'Named' rendering is fine; ensure consistency with 'wonder' vs 'mystery' distinction for '妙' and '玄'.

payload.translation: Le savoir est-il un savoir qui n'est pas le même savoir, le nom est-il un nom qui n'est pas le même nom, le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses, le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse, le désir permet de voir la limite. Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents, ils sont appelés le Sombre. Le Sombre est encore le Sombre, et le Sombre est le commencement des choses.

issues.span: Le savoir est-il un savoir qui n'est pas le même savoir
issues.advice: 道 is 'la Voie' (the Way), not 'le savoir' (knowledge); the opening should render 道可道非常道 as the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way.

issues.span: le nom est-il un nom qui n'est pas le même nom
issues.advice: 名可名非常名 means the name that can be named is not the constant name; the rendering loses the 'constant/eternal' (常) sense.

issues.span: le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: 無名天地之始 means the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth (天地), not 'des choses'.

issues.span: le nom des choses est la mère des choses
issues.advice: 有名萬物之母 means the named is the mother of the ten thousand things (萬物); 'le nom des choses' mistranslates 有名.

issues.span: le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse
issues.advice: 常無欲以觀其妙 means constantly without desire one observes its subtlety/wonder (妙), not 'la sagesse' (wisdom).

issues.span: le désir permet de voir la limite
issues.advice: 常有欲以觀其徼 means constantly with desire one observes its manifestations/boundaries (徼); the '常' (constant) is dropped.

issues.span: le Sombre est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 means the gate of all wonders/marvels, not 'the beginning of things'; 玄之又玄衆妙之門 is mistranslated.

issues.span: le Sombre
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'le Mystère' or 'l'obscur' in Daodejing translations; 'le Sombre' is nonstandard and loses the 'mystery' sense.

issues.span: le savoir
issues.advice: Key term 道 should be 'la Voie'; using 'le savoir' is a serious terminological error for this text.

issues.span: Le savoir est-il un savoir qui n'est pas le même savoir, le nom est-il un nom qui n'est pas le même nom
issues.advice: The repetitive interrogative phrasing is awkward and obscures the parallel structure; render more concisely.

payload.translation: La Voie qui peut être dite n'est pas la Voie qui ne peut être dite ; le Nom qui peut être nommé n'est pas le Nom qui ne peut être nommé ; le Nom sans Nom est le commencement des choses ; le Nom des choses est la mère des choses ; le vide sans désir permet d'observer la sagesse ; le désir permet d'observer les manifestations. Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents ; ils sont appelés le Mystère. Le Mystère est encore le Mystère, et le Mystère est le commencement des choses.

issues.span: le Nom sans Nom est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: Source says 無名 (the nameless) is the beginning of heaven and earth (天地之始), not 'des choses'; and 有名 (the named) is the mother of the ten thousand things (萬物之母). The translation conflates 無名/有名 with 'Nom sans Nom'/'Nom des choses' and misrenders 天地 as 'choses'.

issues.span: le vide sans désir permet d'observer la sagesse
issues.advice: 常無欲以觀其妙 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its subtlety/wonder (妙)', not 'sagesse' (wisdom). 妙 should be rendered as subtlety/merveille, not wisdom.

issues.span: le désir permet d'observer les manifestations
issues.advice: 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly with desire, one observes its manifestations/boundaries (徼)'; the 'constantly' (常) is dropped and the parallel structure with 常無欲 is lost.

issues.span: Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents
issues.advice: 此兩者同出而異名 means 'these two emerge together but have different names'; 'originaires' is not a correct rendering of 同出 (emerge from the same source).

issues.span: le Mystère est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: The final clause 衆妙之門 means 'the gate of all subtleties/wonders', not 'the beginning of things'. This is a mistranslation of 衆妙之門.

issues.span: la Voie qui peut être dite n'est pas la Voie qui ne peut être dite
issues.advice: 常道 is 'the constant/eternal Way', not 'the Way that cannot be said'. The negation 非常道 means 'is not the constant Way'. The rendering inverts the meaning.

issues.span: le Nom qui peut être nommé n'est pas le Nom qui ne peut être nommé
issues.advice: 常名 is 'the constant/eternal Name', not 'the Name that cannot be named'. 非常名 means 'is not the constant Name'.

issues.span: Le Mystère est encore le Mystère, et le Mystère est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 is 'mystery upon mystery' / 'plus mystérieux que le mystère'; the repetition 'est encore le Mystère' is awkward and the appended clause is a mistranslation.

payload.translation: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。常無を欲せず、その妙を見極める。常欲を有して、その境界を見極める。この二つは同一の源から出ているが、異なる名称を持つ。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation wrongly renders it as a prohibition ('should not be mentioned') and drops 非常道/非常名 entirely.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、その妙を見極める。常欲を有して、その境界を見極める。
issues.advice: Source is 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 — 'always without desire, to observe its wonder; always with desire, to observe its boundaries.' The translation negates the first clause (常無を欲せず) and misparses 常無欲/常有欲.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 有名萬物之母 — 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of ten thousand things.' 万物 should be rendered as 万物/万物 (all things), not 万物の母 with 有名 as subject only; acceptable but 万物 mistranslated as generic '万物' is fine—main issue is missing 天地 nuance is minor. Keep as is but ensure 万物 = 万物.

issues.span: これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Source 同謂之玄 玄之又玄 衆妙之門 — 'both are called the mystery; mystery of mysteries, the gate of all wonders.' The translation breaks the syntax; 玄之又玄 should be '玄の又玄' / 'mystery upon mystery' modifying 衆妙の門, not a separate fragment.

issues.span: 常無/常欲
issues.advice: These are key Laozi terms (常無, 常有) meaning 'constant non-being / constant being' or 'always without desire / always with desire'; they should be kept as technical terms, not paraphrased as 常無を欲せず.

issues.span: 玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Fragmentary sentence; should read as a continuous predicate: '玄の又玄、衆妙の門である' or similar.

payload.translation: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。常無を有して、その妙を観ず。常欲を有して、その徼観ず。これら二つは同一の源から出しているが、異なる名称を持つ。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation drops 非常道/非常名 and mistranslates 可道 as a prohibition ('should not be mentioned') rather than a conditional ('can be spoken/expressed').

issues.span: 常無を有して、その妙を観ず。常欲を有して、その徼観ず。
issues.advice: Source is 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 — 'constantly without desire, observe its wonder; constantly with desire, observe its boundaries.' The translation misparses 常無欲 as 常無 + 有, and 徼観ず is ungrammatical/missing を.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である
issues.advice: Source: 無名天地之始、有名萬物之母 — 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of ten thousand things.' Rendering 無名/有名 as bare nouns without the 'nameless/named' sense and omitting 萬物 ('ten thousand things') weakens the terminology.

issues.span: これら二つは同一の源から出しているが
issues.advice: Source 同出而異名 means 'they emerge together but have different names' — 'same source' (同一の源) adds a notion not in the text; render as 同じく出でて名を異にする.

issues.span: 玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄、衆妙之門 — 'mystery upon mystery, the gate of all wonders.' The translation breaks the clause into a fragment and loses the appositive relation; render as 玄の又玄、衆妙の門.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water: it benefits all things without striving; it dwells where others fear; it is good at the depths; it is good at benevolence; it speaks truth; it governs affairs well; it is capable of acting at the right time. For it is because it does not strive.

issues.span: it dwells where others fear
issues.advice: 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that others dislike/despise', not 'fear'. Render as 'dwells where others disdain' or 'in places others detest'.

issues.span: it is good at the depths
issues.advice: 心善淵 means 'its heart/mind is good at (being like) the deep' — the subject is the heart/mind, not water being 'good at depths'. Render as 'its heart is good at depth'.

issues.span: it is good at benevolence
issues.advice: 與善仁 means 'in giving/associating it is good at benevolence' — the parallel structure 居/心/與/言/政/事/動 is lost. Render each as 'in dwelling... in heart... in giving... in speech... in government... in affairs... in action...'.

issues.span: it governs affairs well
issues.advice: 政善治 means 'in government it is good at governing/ordering'; 'governs affairs well' conflates 政 and 事. Keep 政 as 'government' and 事 as 'affairs'.

issues.span: For it is because it does not strive.
issues.advice: 夫惟不爭 is an incomplete clause in the source; the translation drops the concluding sense (故無尤 in the fuller text). At minimum render as 'It is only because it does not strive' — the current 'For it is because' is ungrammatical and incomplete.

issues.span: it is good at the depths; it is good at benevolence; it speaks truth; it governs affairs well; it is capable of acting at the right time
issues.advice: The parallel 善-series is rendered inconsistently (good at / speaks / governs / capable). Use a consistent parallel structure to reflect the classical cadence.

issues.span: The highest virtue
issues.advice: 上善 is conventionally rendered 'the highest good' in Daoist contexts; 'highest virtue' is acceptable but less standard. Consider 'the highest good'.

issues.span: without striving
issues.advice: 不爭 is a key Daoist term often rendered 'without contention' or 'without competing'; 'striving' is acceptable but 'contention' better captures the sense.

payload.translation: The highest good is like water: it benefits all things without contention; it dwells where others disdain; it is good at the depths; it is good in benevolence; it speaks truth; it governs affairs well; it is capable of acting at the right time. For it is only because it does not contend.

issues.span: it is good at the depths
issues.advice: The source 居善地心善淵 contains two parallel clauses: 居善地 (dwelling, it is good at choosing the lowly place) and 心善淵 (in heart/mind, it is good at being deep). The translation merges these and drops 居善地, so render both clauses separately.

issues.span: it governs affairs well
issues.advice: 政善治 refers to governing/administration being well ordered (政, governance), not 'affairs'; and 事善能 (in affairs, it is good at ability/competence) is omitted. Render 政善治 and 事善能 as distinct parallel clauses.

issues.span: For it is only because it does not contend.
issues.advice: The source ends 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not contend), an incomplete clause in the excerpt; the translation adds 'For it is only because' but leaves the causal clause dangling without the implied consequence (故無尤, 'therefore it is without fault'). Either keep it as a faithful fragment or note the ellipsis; do not invent a full stop that changes the sense.

issues.span: it is good at the depths; it is good in benevolence
issues.advice: The chain of 'it is good at/in...' clauses is repetitive and the parallel structure of the original (居/心/與/言/政/事/動 each + 善 + noun) is not preserved. Use varied but parallel phrasing that mirrors the sevenfold structure.

issues.span: the highest good
issues.advice: 上善 is conventionally rendered 'the highest good' or 'supreme good'; acceptable, but ensure consistency with 善 as 'good' throughout (與善仁 = in association, it is good at benevolence).

issues.span: it benefits all things without contention
issues.advice: 水善利萬物而不爭: 不爭 modifies the water's non-contention, not the benefiting; 'benefits all things and does not contend' is closer than 'benefits ... without contention', which slightly shifts the subject of contention.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau : l'eau est utile aux choses sans se battre. Elle habite là où les autres trouvent le malheur, donc elle est proche du Tao. Elle habite le lieu bien choisi, le fond bien profond, la bonté bien généreuse, la parole bien fidèle, la politique bien gouvernée, le travail bien accompli, la capacité bien active, le moment bien choisi. C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.

issues.span: Elle habite le lieu bien choisi, le fond bien profond, la bonté bien généreuse, la parole bien fidèle, la politique bien gouvernée, le travail bien accompli, la capacité bien active, le moment bien ch
issues.advice: The list of 居善地心善淵與善仁言善信政善治事善能動善時 is a series of parallel clauses about the sage's dispositions (dwelling, heart/mind, giving, speech, government, affairs, action, timing), not all governed by 'habite'. Render each with its own verb/noun (e.g. 'il demeure dans un lieu propice, son cœur est un abîme profond, il donne avec bienveillance...') and note 與善仁 means 'in giving, goodness' not 'la bonté bie

issues.span: donc elle est proche du Tao
issues.advice: 故幾於道: 幾 means 'close to/nearly', acceptable, but the causal link 'donc' is fine; ensure 'Tao' consistent with 'la Voie' or keep Tao.

issues.span: C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.
issues.advice: 夫惟不爭 is a concluding clause 'precisely because it does not contend' — the translation drops the emphatic 夫惟 and leaves an incomplete sentence; render as 'C'est justement parce qu'elle ne lutte pas (qu'elle ne peut être blâmée)' or similar complete clause.

issues.span: se bat
issues.advice: 不爭 in Daodejing is conventionally 'ne pas lutter / ne pas rivaliser / ne pas contester'; 'se battre' is too physical. Use 'ne pas lutter' consistently.

issues.span: le travail bien accompli, la capacité bien active
issues.advice: 事善能動善時: 能 is 'ability/efficiency' and 動善時 'in action, good timing'. 'la capacité bien active' is awkward; render as 'dans ses entreprises il est efficace, dans ses mouvements il choisit le bon moment'.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau : l'eau est utile aux choses sans se battre. Elle habite là où les autres trouvent le malheur, donc elle est proche de la Voie. Elle demeure dans un lieu propice, son cœur est un abîme profond, elle donne avec bienveillance, elle parle avec sincérité, elle gouverne avec compétence, elle s'occupe des affaires avec efficacité, elle agit avec intelligence, elle choisit le bon moment. C'est justement parce qu'elle ne lutte pas qu'elle peut être blâmée.

issues.span: elle peut être blâmée
issues.advice: The source ends with 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not contend), with no negation of blame. The rendering 'elle peut être blâmée' ('it can be blamed') inverts the meaning; the clause should express that because it does not contend, it is without fault / nothing can reproach it.

issues.span: elle s'occupe des affaires avec efficacité
issues.advice: 事善能 means 'in affairs, it is capable/effective' — the sense of 能 is capability/ability rather than mere efficiency; consider conveying 'capable' more directly.

issues.span: elle agit avec intelligence
issues.advice: 動善時 means 'in action, it is timely / acts at the right time'; 'avec intelligence' loses the temporal sense of 時. The following 'elle choisit le bon moment' already covers timing, so this clause should reflect timeliness rather than intelligence.

issues.span: elle habite là où les autres trouvent le malheur
issues.advice: 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that people disdain/loathe' — 惡 here is 'to detest/dislike', not 'malheur' (misfortune). Render as places others despise/dislike.

issues.span: Elle demeure dans un lieu propice, son cœur est un abîme profond
issues.advice: The list of parallel clauses (居善地，心善淵…) is rendered with mixed subjects (elle/son cœur) and inconsistent structure; harmonize the parallel construction for readability.

issues.span: 上善如水，利万物而不争。
issues.advice: The source reads 水善利萬物; the translation omits the second 水 and the 善, rendering it as 利万物. Consider preserving 水善利萬物 to match the source's structure.

issues.span: 夫惟不争。
issues.advice: The source ends with 夫惟不争 without a period and is a dependent clause; the added full stop makes it a standalone sentence. Consider keeping it as an open clause consistent with the source.

payload.translation: Carrying wealth to the point of excess is not as good as stopping it; sharpening one's mind is not as beneficial as not sharpening it; guarding wealth and gold is not as secure as not guarding it; having a full treasury and being rich is not as safe as not being rich; being proud and forgetting one's mistakes is not as good as not forgetting one's mistakes; achieving success and fame is not as good as not achieving it; retiring from the world is not as good as not retiring; the way of heaven is to let things be as they are.

issues.span: sharpening one's mind is not as beneficial as not sharpening it
issues.advice: The source 揣而銳之 means 'hammering/sharpening something to make it sharp' — the object is a blade or point, not 'one's mind'; the clause warns that a sharpened edge cannot be preserved long (不可長保), which the translation omits entirely.

issues.span: guarding wealth and gold is not as secure as not guarding it; having a full treasury and being rich is not as safe as not being rich
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, yet none can keep them' — a single clause, not two separate comparisons; the translation invents parallel 'not as good as not...' structures absent from the source.

issues.span: being proud and forgetting one's mistakes is not as good as not forgetting one's mistakes
issues.advice: 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance bring self-inflicted disaster' (自遺其咎 = one brings the blame on oneself); 'forgetting one's mistakes' is a mistranslation of 咎 (fault/calamity).

issues.span: achieving success and fame is not as good as not achieving it; retiring from the world is not as good as not retiring
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退天之道 is one statement: 'when merit is accomplished and fame achieved, to withdraw the self — that is the way of heaven.' It is not a comparison nor a rejection of success; 身退 means withdrawing oneself, not 'retiring from the world.'

issues.span: the way of heaven is to let things be as they are
issues.advice: 天之道 here concludes the passage as 'the way of heaven' attached to the withdrawal clause; 'to let things be as they are' is an added interpretation not present in the source.

issues.span: Carrying wealth to the point of excess
issues.advice: 持而盈之 means 'holding and filling to the brim' — overfilling a vessel — not specifically 'carrying wealth'; the wealth reading is imported from later clauses.

issues.span: is not as good as stopping it; ... is not as beneficial as not sharpening it; ... is not as secure as not guarding it; ... is not as safe as not being rich; ... is not as good as not forgetting one's
issues.advice: The repeated mechanical 'is not as good as not...' pattern is monotonous and distorts the aphoristic parallel structure of the original; vary the construction to reflect the classical rhetorical form.

issues.span: retiring from the world
issues.advice: 身退 in the Daodejing context refers to withdrawing from position/credit after success, not world-renunciation; render the cultural concept of timely self-withdrawal accurately.

payload.translation: To hold wealth to excess is not as good as holding it to its limit; to sharpen one's mind is not as beneficial as not sharpening it; to guard wealth and gold is not as secure as not guarding them; to have a full treasury and be rich is not as safe as not being rich; to be proud and forget one's faults is not as good as not forgetting one's faults; to achieve merit and fame is not as good as not achieving them; to withdraw from the world is not as good as not withdrawing; the way of heaven is to let things be as they are.

issues.span: to hold wealth to excess is not as good as holding it to its limit
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and fill it to overflowing is not as good as stopping in time'; 'holding it to its limit' reverses the meaning and 'wealth' is not in the source.

issues.span: to sharpen one's mind is not as beneficial as not sharpening it
issues.advice: 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'to hammer and sharpen it to a point cannot be kept long'; the translation invents 'mind' and 'beneficial' and drops the sense of impermanence.

issues.span: to guard wealth and gold is not as secure as not guarding them
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, yet none can keep them'; the translation adds a comparative 'not as secure as not guarding' that is not in the source.

issues.span: to have a full treasury and be rich is not as safe as not being rich
issues.advice: This sentence is not in the source at all; it is an invented line.

issues.span: to be proud and forget one's faults is not as good as not forgetting one's faults
issues.advice: 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'to be rich and noble yet arrogant is to bring disaster upon oneself'; 'forget one's faults' mistranslates 自遺其咎.

issues.span: to achieve merit and fame is not as good as not achieving them
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退天之道 means 'when merit is achieved and fame accomplished, to withdraw the self is the way of heaven'; it is not a comparative about not achieving fame.

issues.span: to withdraw from the world is not as good as not withdrawing

issues.span: Levantant-leur, ne sont-ils pas comme si l'argent était plein et ne suffisait pas à l'usage?
issues.advice: The opening 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and fill it is not as good as stopping' — a counsel against overfilling, not a rhetorical question about money being insufficient. Render as a declarative maxim.

issues.span: Leurs ardeurs ne sont-elles pas comme si elles ne pouvaient pas être conservées?
issues.advice: 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'hammering it sharp, it cannot be preserved long' — a metaphor about sharpness not lasting, not 'ardeurs'. Keep the image of sharpening and the idea of not enduring.

issues.span: Les richesses et les biens ne sont-ils pas remplis dans les palais, mais ne peuvent-ils être tenus? Les richesses et les biens ne sont-elles pas les plus abondantes, mais ne peuvent-ils pas être gardé
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂莫之能守 is a single line: 'gold and jade fill the hall, none can guard them.' The translation duplicates it into two redundant rhetorical questions and drops 'or et jade'. Consolidate into one declarative sentence.

issues.span: Le succès de la fortune et du prestige ne sont-ils pas les plus brillants, mais ne peuvent-ils pas être conservés?
issues.advice: 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance bring self-inflicted blame.' The translation turns this into another rhetorical question about preservation and omits the key notion of self-caused fault (咎).

issues.span: L'homme qui s'enorgueillit de ses succès et qui s'enflamme de gloire se perd en lui-même.
issues.advice: This sentence is misplaced: it renders 富貴而驕自遺其咎 but appears after the line that should correspond to it, and adds 's'enflamme de gloire' not in the source. Reorder and remove the addition.

issues.span: La nature du ciel est que le succès ne soit pas conservé, et la gloire ne soit pas gardée.
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退天之道 means 'when the work is done and name achieved, withdraw the body — this is the way of heaven.' The translation omits 身退 (withdrawal/retirement) entirely and negates the sense. Render as: success achieved, then retire; that is heaven's way.

issues.span: Levantant-leur
issues.advice: 'Levantant' is not a French word; the participle is 'levant'. Also the pronoun 'leur' has no antecedent.

issues.span: ne sont-ils pas ... ne peuvent-ils pas
issues.advice: The repeated interrogative-negative construction is unnatural for a classical aphorism; use declarative maxims in French.

issues.span: la nature du ciel
issues.advice: 天之道 is conventionally 'la voie du ciel' (the Way of Heaven), not 'la nature du ciel'.

issues.span: l'argent
issues.advice: 金玉 is 'or et jade' (gold and jade); 'argent' (silver/money) is inaccurate.

issues.span: c'est la voie du ciel
issues.advice: '天之道' applies specifically to the final clause '功成名遂身退' (withdrawal after success is the way of heaven), not to the whole preceding list; the causal link is misattributed.

payload.translation: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり、金玉は満堂に充れども守らざるなり、富貴は驕して遺すなり、功は成り名は遂れ、身は退くなり、天の道なり。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず
issues.advice: 原文「不如其已」は「むしろやめたほうがよい」の意。訳文は「止むを得ず（やむを得ない）」と逆の意味になっている。比較表現「不如」を「〜に如かず」と捉え直す必要がある。

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: 「不可長保」は「長く保つことはできない」の否定。訳文は「長きものなり」と肯定になっており意味が反転している。

issues.span: 金玉は満堂に充れども守らざるなり
issues.advice: 「莫之能守」は「これを守ること能わず」で、誰も守れないという不可能の意。「守らざるなり（守らない）」では意味が異なる。

issues.span: 富貴は驕して遺すなり
issues.advice: 「自遺其咎」は「自らその咎を遺す」で、驕ることが災いを自ら招く意。「遺す」だけでは咎（災い）の目的語が抜けている。

issues.span: 身は退くなり
issues.advice: 「身退」は「身を退く」で引退する意。「退くなり」は禁止・命令のように読め誤り。已然形・連体形の整理が必要。

issues.span: 揣て
issues.advice: 「揣」は漢文訓読では通常「はかりて」と読む。送り仮名「て」のみでは不適切。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: 四字句の対句構造が崩れ、接続が不自然。漢文訓読としてのリズムと係り結びを整える必要がある。

issues.span: 天の道なり
issues.advice: 『老子』の定型句「天之道」は訓読慣例で「天の道なり」と読む点は可だが、全体が訓読体として統一されておらず、古典受容の文体として不整合。

payload.translation: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり、金玉は満堂に充れども守らざるなり、富貴は驕して自ら咎を遺すなり、功は成り、名は遂れ、身は退くなり、天の道なり。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず
issues.advice: 原文は「持而盈之不如其已」で、満ちるまで保つより止める方がよいという比較の意味。訳は「止むを得ず」（やむを得ない）となっており意味が逆転している。不如其已は「その已むに如かず」と訳すべき。

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: 原文は「揣而銳之不可長保」で、鋭くしたものは長く保てないという否定。訳は「長きものなり」と肯定になっており、不可長保の否定が失われている。「長く保つべからず」とすべき。

issues.span: 金玉は満堂に充れども守らざるなり
issues.advice: 原文「莫之能守」は誰も守り通せないという意味。訳の「守らざるなり」は守らないという能動的否定で意味が異なる。「之を守る能うもの莫し」とすべき。

issues.span: 富貴は驕して自ら咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: 原文「富貴而驕自遺其咎」は富貴でありながら驕ることが自ら咎を残すという因果。訳は富貴と驕が並列に読め、因果関係が不明瞭。「富貴にして驕れば自ら其の咎を遺す」とすべき。

issues.span: 功は成り、名は遂れ、身は退くなり
issues.advice: 原文「功成名遂身退」は功成り名遂げて身退くという条件・時系列の関係。訳の「身は退くなり」は断定・命令のように読め、「天の道なり」とのつながりも不自然。「功成り名遂げて身退く、是れ天の道なり」とすべき。

issues.span: 揣て
issues.advice: 「揣」は漢文的に「揣（はか）る」と読むが、日本語として不自然で送り仮名も不適切。「揣（はか）りて」または「鋭く錬れば」など文脈に即した表現にすべき。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: 文語体として不自然で、原文の対句構造も崩れている。漢文訓読調のリズムに整えるべき。

payload.translation: The wise who have skillfully cultivated the Way are subtle, mysterious, and comprehensively profound, yet deeply unrecognizable. It is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they cultivate a gentle demeanor, like a traveler crossing a river in winter, or like fearing one's four neighbors. They appear composed as if they were a guest, dispersed as if the ice were melting, and pure as the unadulterated wood. They are vast as the open sky, and like the valley. They are all-encompassing as if they were turbid. Who can make turbidity still? Who can slowly clear it? Who can make things quiet? Who can make things endure? The one who preserves this Way does not wish to be full. It is precisely because they are not full that they can endure without being renewed.

issues.span: that they cultivate a gentle demeanor
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; 彊 (qiǎng) means 'forced/constrained', not 'cultivate'. The translation reverses the logic and mistranslates 容 as demeanor to be cultivated.

issues.span: 豫若冬涉川
issues.advice: 豫 (yù) means hesitant/cautious, 'as if crossing a river in winter' — the translation renders it as 'a traveler crossing a river in winter', losing the hesitation nuance and adding 'traveler'.

issues.span: 猶若畏四鄰
issues.advice: 猶 (yóu) means 'cautious/wary', parallel to 豫; 'or like fearing one's four neighbors' breaks the parallel structure and adds 'or'.

issues.span: 敦兮其若樸
issues.advice: 敦 (dūn) means 'simple/sincere/uncarved', not 'pure'; 樸 is 'uncarved wood/plainness', not 'unadulterated wood'.

issues.span: 曠兮其若谷
issues.advice: 曠 means 'open/vast/spacious', rendered as 'vast as the open sky' — 谷 is 'valley', so the simile should be 'open like a valley', not 'open sky'.

issues.span: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生
issues.advice: The two parallel rhetorical questions are mistranslated: 'Who can make turbidity still? Who can slowly clear it? Who can make things quiet? Who can make things endure?' The source asks: who can, being turbid, still it and slowly clear it; who can, being at rest, long move it and slowly generate life. The second clause 安以乆動之徐生 is omitted/misrendered.

issues.span: 故能弊不新成
issues.advice: 弊 (bì) here means 'worn/old' and 不新成 means 'not newly completed/made new' — i.e., they can be worn out without needing renewal. The translation 'endure without being renewed' inverts the sense.

issues.span: the Way
issues.advice: 道 in this Daoist context is conventionally rendered 'the Way' (capitalized) — acceptable — but 士 is 'the true man/master/scholar', not merely 'the wise'; consider 'the masters of old who were skilled in the Way'.

issues.span: comprehensively profound
issues.advice: 玄通 means 'mysteriously penetrating/pervasive'; 'comprehensively profound' is awkward and inaccurate.

issues.span: They are all-encompassing as if they were turbid
issues.advice: 渾兮 means 'simple/undifferentiated/muddy-like'; 'all-encompassing' is a mistranslation and the sentence is awkward.

issues.span: gentle demeanor
issues.advice: The passage is a classic Daoist description of the sage's ineffable character; the translation's psychologizing ('cultivate a gentle demeanor') loses the classical rhetorical structure of 彊為之容 (forced description).

payload.translation: The masters of old who skillfully cultivated the Way were subtle, mysterious, and penetratingly profound, yet deeply unrecognizable. It is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they cultivate a gentle demeanor, like a traveler crossing a river in winter, or like fearing one's four neighbors. They appear composed as if they were a guest, dispersed as if the ice were melting, and simple as the uncarved wood. They are vast as the open sky, and like the valley. They are all-encompassing as if they were turbid. Who can make turbidity still? Who can slowly clear it? Who can make things quiet? Who can make things endure? The one who preserves this Way does not wish to be full. It is precisely because they are not full that they can endure without being renewed.

issues.span: they cultivate a gentle demeanor
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; 彊為 means 'forced to/compelled to', not 'cultivate'. Render as 'one is forced to describe their appearance'.

issues.span: Who can make turbidity still? Who can slowly clear it? Who can make things quiet? Who can make things endure?
issues.advice: The source 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, amid turbidity, still it and slowly clarify it? Who can, amid stability, long activate it and slowly give life?' The translation splits and distorts the parallel structure; 安以乆動之徐生 is mistranslated as 'make things quiet/endure'.

issues.span: they can endure without being renewed
issues.advice: The source 故能弊不新成 means 'therefore they can be worn out without needing new completion' or 'can remain worn without being newly made'. 'endure without being renewed' misses 弊 (worn/old) and 新成 (newly completed).

issues.span: vast as the open sky
issues.advice: 曠兮其若谷 means 'open/vast like a valley', not 'open sky'. The valley image is lost.

issues.span: the Way
issues.advice: For 道 in Daodejing context, 'the Way' is acceptable, but consistency with 士 (the masters) is fine; no change needed—flagging only for consistency.

issues.span: or like fearing one's four neighbors
issues.advice: 猶若畏四鄰 means 'hesitant as if fearing neighboring states'; 'fearing one's four neighbors' is awkward and unclear. Render 'as if wary of the four neighboring states'.

issues.span: They are all-encompassing as if they were turbid
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/undifferentiated like muddy water'; 'all-encompassing' is an interpretive addition not in the source.

payload.translation: Ceux qui savent bien faire le sage sont subtils, mystérieux, et profondément incompréhensibles. C'est parce qu'ils sont incompréhensibles qu'ils se montrent doucement et tranquilles. Comme l'on traverse une rivière en hiver, comme on craint les quatre voisins, comme un étranger, comme l'eau qui se dissout, comme de la pierre brute, comme un champ vide. Tout est un mélange, comme le trouble. Qui peut rendre le trouble calme ? Et qui peut calmer le trouble ? Et qui peut s'arrêter longtemps dans le mouvement ? Le seul qui garde cette voie n'est pas plein. C'est parce qu'il n'est pas plein qu'il ne se dégrade pas, qu'il ne se renouvelle pas.

issues.span: Ceux qui savent bien faire le sage
issues.advice: The source 古之善為士者 means 'those in antiquity who were skilled in being a true practitioner/master (士)', not 'those who know how to make the sage'. Render as 'Ceux qui, dans l'antiquité, excellaient à être des maîtres (士)'.

issues.span: ils se montrent doucement et tranquilles
issues.advice: 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; it is not about them appearing gently/calmly. Render as 'c'est pourquoi l'on est contraint de décrire leur apparence'.

issues.span: comme l'eau qui se dissout
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 = 'dissolving like ice about to melt'. The image is ice melting, not water dissolving. Render 'comme la glace sur le point de fondre'.

issues.span: comme de la pierre brute, comme un champ vide
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸 = 'simple/uncarved like unworked wood (樸)'; 曠兮其若谷 = 'vast/open like a valley (谷)'. 'pierre brute' and 'champ vide' misread the images. Render 'comme le bois non travaillé' and 'comme une vallée'.

issues.span: Tout est un mélange, comme le trouble. Qui peut rendre le trouble calme ? Et qui peut calmer le trouble ?
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 = 'mixed/turbid like muddy water'. The rhetorical pair 孰能濁以靜之徐清 / 孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness, gradually clarify? Who can, from rest, by long movement, gradually generate life?' The translation duplicates 'calmer le trouble' and omits the gradual clarification and the generation from movement. Render both clauses distinctly with 徐 = 'peu à peu'.

issues.span: Et qui peut s'arrêter longtemps dans le mouvement ?
issues.advice: 安以乆動之徐生 = 'who can, from rest, by prolonged movement, gradually bring forth life?' It is not 'stop long in movement'. Render 'Qui peut, du repos, par un long mouvement, faire naître peu à peu la vie ?'.

issues.span: qu'il ne se dégrade pas, qu'il ne se renouvelle pas
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 = 'thus he can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed/made new' — i.e., he endures worn without requiring renewal. The negation is misplaced: it should be 'il peut être usé sans se renouveler/être refait à neuf', not 'il ne se dégrade pas'.

issues.span: le sage
issues.advice: 士 here is the Daoist practitioner/master, not simply 'le sage' (which would be 聖人). Use 'le maître' or 'le véritable homme'.

issues.span: cette voie
issues.advice: 道 should be rendered consistently as 'la Voie' (capitalized) in Daoist context.

issues.span: subtils, mystérieux, et profondément incompréhensibles
issues.advice: Comma before 'et' is unidiomatic in French; also the string of adjectives is awkward. Smooth as 'subtils, mystérieux, pénétrants et profondément insondables'.

issues.span: comme on craint les quatre voisins
issues.advice: 猶若畏四鄰 = 'hesitant as if fearing the four neighbors'. The 'comme on craint' clause lacks the hesitant nuance (猶) and reads as a bare comparison; render 'hésitant comme celui qui craint ses quatre voisins'.

issues.span: les quatre voisins
issues.advice: 四鄰 is a set phrase meaning neighboring states/people on all four sides; 'les quatre voisins' is literal but opaque. Consider 'les voisins de tous côtés' to convey the idiom.

payload.translation: Ceux qui, dans l'antiquité, excellaient à être des maîtres (士) sont subtils, mystérieux, pénétrants et profondément insondables. C'est pourquoi l'on est contraint de décrire leur apparence : ils sont hésitant comme celui qui craint ses quatre voisins, comme s'il se trouvait sur le point de fondre, comme du bois non travaillé, comme une vallée. Tout est un mélange, comme le trouble. Qui peut, du trouble, par une action lente, rendre le trouble calme ? Qui peut, du repos, par un long mouvement, faire naître peu à peu la vie ? Le seul qui garde cette voie n'est pas plein. C'est parce qu'il n'est pas plein qu'il ne se dégrade pas, qu'il ne se renouvelle pas.

issues.span: ils sont hésitant comme celui qui craint ses quatre voisins
issues.advice: The source has two distinct similes: 豫若冬涉川 (hesitant like one crossing a river in winter) and 猶若畏四鄰 (cautious like one fearing the four neighbors). The first simile (winter river crossing) is omitted and the two are conflated; restore both images separately.

issues.span: comme s'il se trouvait sur le point de fondre
issues.advice: Source 渙若冰將釋 means 'yielding/dissolving like ice about to melt'; the ice image is dropped. Render the melting-ice simile explicitly.

issues.span: Tout est un mélange, comme le trouble
issues.advice: Source 渾兮其若濁 describes the master as 'chaotic/unrefined like muddy water'; the translation turns it into a general statement ('Tout est un mélange') and loses the subject. Keep it as a description of the person.

issues.span: par une action lente, rendre le trouble calme
issues.advice: Source 濁以靜之徐清 means 'by stillness, gradually clarify the muddy'; 'action lente' misreads 靜 (stillness) as action. Use 'par le calme/la quiétude'.

issues.span: qu'il ne se dégrade pas, qu'il ne se renouvelle pas
issues.advice: Source 能弊不新成 means 'can remain worn/old without needing new completion' — i.e., he does not seek renewal. The rendering 'ne se dégrade pas' adds a sense of decay not present; reconsider as 'il peut demeurer usé sans se renouveler'.

issues.span: des maîtres (士)
issues.advice: Glossing the Chinese character in parentheses is not appropriate in a finished translation; render 士 as 'les hommes de valeur/les sages' without the source-character gloss.

issues.span: ils sont hésitant
issues.advice: Agreement error: 'hésitants' (plural) to agree with 'ils'.

issues.span: comme celui qui craint ses quatre voisins, comme s'il se trouvait sur le point de fondre, comme du bois non travaillé, comme une vallée
issues.advice: The chain of 'comme' clauses is repetitive and the referents shift awkwardly; restructure so each simile clearly modifies the masters and reads naturally in French.

payload.translation: 古に善く人を修める者は微妙玄通深く不可知なり。夫は不可知なるため、強いてその容儀を設め、豫かに振る舞う。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客に似て、氷が解けるように、朴（樸）なるように、広く、谷（谷）なるように、混み（濁）なるように。誰が静かに濁りを清めるか。徐々にして清める。誰が動いて安らぎ、久しく動かすか。徐々にして生保する。この道に善く生きる者は、盈（満）なることを避け、夫は不盈（不満）なるため、弊（弊）を新（新）く成る。

issues.span: 善く人を修める者は
issues.advice: 「善為士者」は「士（すぐれた人物）をよく修める者」ではなく「古の道をよく修めた士（すぐれた人物）」の意。主客が逆転している。

issues.span: 強いてその容儀を設め
issues.advice: 「彊為之容」は「しいてその容（すがた・ありさま）を形容する」の意で、「容儀を設ける」は不適切。

issues.span: 混み（濁）なるように
issues.advice: 「渾兮其若濁」は「渾然として濁れるがごとし」の意。「混みなる」は日本語として不自然で意味も不正確。

issues.span: 誰が静かに濁りを清めるか。徐々にして清める。
issues.advice: 「孰能濁以靜之徐清」は「誰か濁れるを静めて徐かに清からしめうる」の意。問いと答えの構造が崩れ、主語・目的語が不明瞭。

issues.span: 誰が動いて安らぎ、久しく動かすか。徐々にして生保する。
issues.advice: 「孰能安以乆動之徐生」は「誰か安きを久しくして徐かに動きて生ぜしめうる」の意。「生保する」は原文にない語で誤訳。

issues.span: この道に善く生きる者は
issues.advice: 「保此道者」は「この道を保つ者は」の意。「善く生きる者」は原文にない解釈の付加。

issues.span: 弊（弊）を新（新）く成る
issues.advice: 「故能弊不新成」は「ゆえに弊（やぶ）れても新たに成さず（新成を求めず）」の意。訳文は意味不明で、原文の否定構造「不新成」が反映されていない。

issues.span: 盈（満）なることを避け、夫は不盈（不満）なるため
issues.advice: 「不欲盈」「不盈」は「盈（み）つるを欲せず」「盈たざるがゆえに」であり、「不満」という心理的語は不適切。老子の術語として「盈」を保つべき。

issues.span: 豫かに振る舞う。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客に似て、氷が解けるように、朴（樸）なるように、広く、谷（谷）なるように
issues.advice: 「豫若冬渉川、猶若畏四隣、儼若客、渙若氷将釈、敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷」の並列比喩が崩れ、文が断片的。各句を「〜のごとし」で統一すべき。

issues.span: 谷（谷）
issues.advice: 「谷」に同字の注記を付すのは無意味。老子の「谷」は虚空・謙下の象徴であり、原語をそのまま用いるか注釈で補うべき。

payload.translation: 古の善く道を修めた者は微妙玄通深く不可知なり。夫は不可知なるため、強いてその容儀を設め、豫かに振る舞う。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客に似て、氷が解けるように、朴（樸）なるように、曠（曠）なるように、谷（谷）なるように、渾（混）然として濁れるがごとし。誰が静かに濁りを清めるか。徐々にして清からしめうる。誰が動いて安らぎ、久しく動かすか。徐々にして生保する。この道に善く生きる者は、盈（満）つるを欲せず、夫は不盈（不満）なるため、弊（やぶ）れても新たに成さず。

issues.span: 誰が静かに濁りを清めるか。徐々にして清からしめうる。
issues.advice: The rhetorical question 孰能濁以靜之徐清 means 'who can, being turbid, quiet it and slowly clarify it?' The translation splits it awkwardly and the second sentence ('徐々にして清からしめうる') misrenders the causative/gradual sense; the subject and the 'by quieting' relation are lost.

issues.span: 誰が動いて安らぎ、久しく動かすか。徐々にして生保する。
issues.advice: 孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'who can, being at rest, through long movement slowly bring forth life?' The rendering '久しく動かす' and '生保する' distort the sense (生保 is not the meaning; it should be 'slowly generate/produce life').

issues.span: この道に善く生きる者は
issues.advice: 保此道者 means 'one who preserves/keeps this Way', not 'one who lives well in this Way'. 保 = preserve/hold.

issues.span: 弊（やぶ）れても新たに成さず
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed/made new' — i.e., can endure decay rather than seek renewal. The rendering '新たに成さず' is ambiguous and loses the sense that the sage does not seek new completion.

issues.span: 豫かに振る舞う。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客に似て
issues.advice: The four similes 豫/猶/儼/渙 are parallel: 'hesitant as if crossing a river in winter; cautious as if fearing neighbors; dignified as if a guest; yielding as if ice about to melt'. The translation breaks the parallel structure and drops 渙若冰將釋 into the list without its 'as if melting' sense.

issues.span: 朴（樸）なるように、曠（曠）なるように、谷（谷）なるように
issues.advice: Redundant parenthetical glosses (朴（樸）, 曠（曠）, 谷（谷）) are not idiomatic Japanese and repeat the same character; remove the glosses and render the similes naturally.

issues.span: 渾（混）然として濁れるがごとし
issues.advice: The gloss 渾（混）is unnecessary and the phrase is awkward; render 渾兮其若濁 as '混然として濁っているかのよう'.

issues.span: 夫は不可知なるため
issues.advice: 夫惟 here is a classical connective ('only because'), not the demonstrative 夫; rendering it as '夫は' misreads the particle and reads unnaturally in Japanese.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been going on for more than two years. Yet, while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling, which shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a person, so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people. Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear, and finally it all reduces to transmitting Ah Q, as if there were a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has been going on for more than two years
issues.advice: The source says 已经不止一两年了 (more than one or two years / not just a year or two), which is vaguer and longer than 'more than two years'; render as 'more than a year or two' to preserve the original's imprecision.

issues.span: while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling
issues.advice: 往回想 means 'to think back / reconsider / have second thoughts', not merely 'recalling'; the sense of hesitation/reconsideration is lost. Convey the backward-looking hesitation.

issues.span: establishing words
issues.advice: 『立言』 is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words/leaving a lasting saying as one of the three immortalities); a literal gloss without context loses the allusion. Consider a rendering that signals the classical allusion, e.g. 'a man who establishes words (li yan)'.

issues.span: so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people
issues.advice: The source 人以文传，文以人传 is a chiastic pair meaning 'the person is transmitted through the writing, the writing through the person'; the current rendering reverses the order and flattens the rhetorical structure. Preserve the chiasmus.

issues.span: finally it all reduces to transmitting Ah Q
issues.advice: 归结到传阿Q means 'it finally comes down to writing the biography of Ah Q', not 'transmitting Ah Q'; 传 here is 'to write a biography', consistent with 正传 in the opening.

issues.span: Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear
issues.advice: Remove the comma after 'whom' (subject-verb interruption) and smooth the clause.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been going on for more than a year or two. Yet, while I am writing, I am also constantly thinking back, which shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a person, so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people. Ultimately, who transmits whom has become increasingly unclear, and finally it all comes down to writing Ah Q's biography, as if there were a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been going on for more than a year or two
issues.advice: The source says the intention/plan to write has lasted more than a year or two (已经不止一两年了), not that the writing itself has been ongoing. Render as something like 'It has been more than a year or two that I have wanted to write a biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: "establishing words"
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian concept (the 'three immortalities': 立德, 立功, 立言). A literal gloss like 'establishing words' is opaque; consider a rendering that conveys 'one who establishes words/leaves a lasting saying' or add a brief gloss.

issues.span: For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a person
issues.advice: The source 从来不朽之笔，须传不朽之人 means an immortal pen must transmit/hand down an immortal person — the pen does not 'immortalize' the person; the person is already immortal. Adjust to 'an immortal pen must transmit an immortal person.'

issues.span: so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people
issues.advice: The source 人以文传，文以人传 is a chiastic pair: 'the person is handed down through the writing, and the writing is handed down through the person.' The current phrasing loses the passive 'is transmitted/handed down' sense and reads as if people actively transmit.

issues.span: as if there were a ghost in my thoughts
issues.advice: Acceptable, but 仿佛思想里有鬼似的 is more idiomatically 'as if a ghost were haunting my mind/thoughts.' Minor.

payload.translation: Aq was not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague; even his former deeds were vague. For the people of Wuzhuang, as to Aq, it was enough that he helped them, or they made a joke of him; they never took notice of his deeds. Aq himself did not say so, but only when he quarreled with others, he would sometimes stare into the sky and say: "We were once much richer than you! What are you?"

issues.span: Aq was not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague
issues.advice: The source means 'Not only were Ah Q's name and native place somewhat vague'; the translation's structure misattributes vagueness. Restructure so 'name and place of origin' are the subject of 'vague'.

issues.span: as to Aq, it was enough that he helped them, or they made a joke of him
issues.advice: Source says they only wanted him to help and only made jokes of him (只要...只...), not 'it was enough that...or'. Render as 'they only wanted him to help them and only made fun of him'.

issues.span: Aq himself did not say so
issues.advice: Source 阿Q自己也不说 means 'Ah Q himself did not talk about it/never mentioned it', not 'did not say so'. Use 'Ah Q himself never mentioned it'.

issues.span: stare into the sky
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means 'glare/glower with wide eyes', not 'stare into the sky'. Use 'glare' or 'stare wide-eyed'.

issues.span: Wuzhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' (or 'the Village of Wei'); 'Wuzhuang' is a mistransliteration.

issues.span: Aq
issues.advice: The character is conventionally 'Ah Q' in English translations; use 'Ah Q'.

issues.span: deeds
issues.advice: 『行状』 (quoted term) refers to one's 'record/background/exploits'; consider 'record' or 'exploits' consistently, and note the quotation marks.

issues.span: We were once much richer than you!
issues.advice: 我们先前——比你阔的多啦 conveys 'In the past we were much better off than you'; 'richer' is acceptable but 'better off' is more idiomatic; also the dash emphasis is lost.

payload.translation: Ah Q was not only his name and native place somewhat vague; even his former deeds were vague. For the people of Weizhuang, as to Ah Q, it was enough that he helped them, or they only made fun of him; they never took notice of his record. Ah Q himself never mentioned it, but only when he quarreled with others, he would sometimes glare with wide eyes and say: "We were once much better off than you! What are you?"

issues.span: Ah Q was not only his name and native place somewhat vague
issues.advice: The construction is garbled; the source means 'Not only were Ah Q's name and native place somewhat vague' — the subject-predicate order is inverted, producing an ungrammatical sentence.

issues.span: For the people of Weizhuang, as to Ah Q, it was enough that he helped them, or they only made fun of him
issues.advice: The source says the villagers only wanted him to help and only made fun of him (只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑); 'it was enough that... or' misrepresents the parallel structure and adds a false alternative.

issues.span: Weizhuang
issues.advice: The conventional rendering of 未庄 in Lu Xun translations is 'Weizhuang' but should be consistent; more importantly 行状 is rendered inconsistently as 'deeds' and 'record' — pick one consistent term (e.g., 'record'/'biography').

issues.span: We were once much better off than you!
issues.advice: 『我们先前——比你阔的多啦』 means 'we were once far richer/more prosperous than you'; 'much better off' weakens 阔 (wealthy/rich) and the emphatic 多啦.

issues.span: but only when he quarreled with others, he would sometimes glare
issues.advice: The 'but only when...he would' clause is awkward; restructure so the temporal clause reads naturally (e.g., 'only occasionally, when quarreling...').
